rationale: Marketing social post deploys explicitly forbidden buzzwords ('miracle', 'guilt-free', 'guaranteed') in violation of brand voice guidelines.
Social media copy asserts unapproved clinical cognitive enhancement claims ('scientifically proven to improve focus and memory') violating claim restrictions.
Influencer marketing post lacks mandatory commercial sponsorship disclosure (#ad or Paid Partnership) required by statutory guidelines.
Promotional web copy hallucinates non-existent ingredients (Himalayan Pink Salt, Madagascar Vanilla, organic almond butter) absent from verified product specs.
Email newsletter contains two severe blocking violations: false 'sugar-free' claim (product has 4g added sugar) and illegal disease prevention claim.
Promotional social post cites obsolete quantity terms from superseded campaign brief (6 jars instead of current approved 4 jars).
Marketing copy targets children with prohibited cognitive growth and developmental promises in direct violation of claims register.
Packaging panel contains a direct nutritional contradiction: states 10 g protein per 30 g serving when certified lab specification is 6 g.
Product packaging asserts the snack serves as a complete meal replacement, violating explicit statutory claim restrictions.
E-commerce product specification asserts a revoked 100% nut-free claim, creating severe consumer allergy safety hazards.
Packaging copy hallucinates count and net weight (12 bites / 100 g) conflicting with certified manufacturing specs (6 bites / 60 g).
Product catalog understates sugar content as 1 g when verified lab tests certify 4 g added sugar per serving.
Packaging claims USDA Organic and Non-GMO Project Verified seals that are unapproved and pending certification.
Initially evaluated as generic commercial puffery ('leading energy bar brands') without naming a direct competitor brand.
Corporate press release draft hallucinates a non-existent $150M Series C funding round and fabricated venture capital investors.
Direct violation of enterprise accessibility policy SRC-POLICY-01 which forbids bypassing WCAG 2.1 AA audits for all software releases.
Commercial RFP response makes an unauthorized 99.999% delivery SLA guarantee exceeding contractual logistics capacity (98.5%).
Investor presentation cites expired 2024 carbon neutrality credentials as active, misleading stakeholders.
Corporate release uses rejected trademark mark (SuperOat™) and banned superlative ('miracle') in violation of trademark and voice registers.
Enterprise vendor portal publishes fictitious ISO 22000 certification and misidentifies safety rating level and auditing registrar.
Marketing social post strictly adheres to approved claim register ('cocoa oat snack for everyday moments', 'made with wholegrain oats') and approved voice.
Website headline and copy accurately reflect certified serving size, protein content (6 g), and added sugar (4 g) from approved specifications.
Social ad highlights approved bite count (six bites per pack) and aligns with approved target audience and tone.
Email newsletter uses approved claim '6 g protein per 30 g serving' with compliant, non-absolute lifestyle framing.
Product packaging front-panel copy incorporates approved allergen disclosure, flavor identifier, and serving size.
E-commerce product specification page accurately lists ingredients and approved nutritional facts.
Retail packaging back-panel text includes verified claim registry statements with zero unauthorized embellishments.
Corporate press release describes regional retail distribution expansion in neutral, factual, and verified terms.
B2B wholesale partner portal accurately specifies case pack configurations and unit net weights from operational inventory facts.
Internal compliance bulletin reaffirms verified corporate accessibility policy and approved disclosure procedures.
